1.0 ABOUT THIS DOCUMENT

1.1 Purpose

This document is the detailed specification of Sketchpad Version 2 ("V2"). It expands every requirement of the functional specification, SPV2-FS-001 Revision B ("the FS"), to the level at which it could be built and tested: the exact data formats, every interface between parts, the algorithms, the limits, the error cases, and an acceptance test for each requirement. It is written to be read by people who have not seen Sketchpad, so that they can analyse the design, find its weaknesses, and say where it should change before construction starts.

Where the FS says what, this document says how exactly and how we will know. Where the two differ, the FS governs and this document is in error; please report it.

1.2 How to read it

  • Section 2 is the context: who the owner is, what he makes, and the constraints the design must respect. Read it first; much of the design follows from it.
  • Sections 3 to 16 specify the parts, in the order data flows through them: the kernel, generators and settings, documents, commands, session, storage, the script host, rendering and output, and then the cross-cutting parts (commands table, errors, Sweep, journals, regression, robustness).
  • Section 17 gives the non-functional requirements; section 18 the migration from V1; section 19 the construction and test plan; section 20 the risks and the questions for analysts; section 21 the requirement index.

1.3 Conventions

As in the FS: "shall" is a requirement, "should" a recommendation, "may" an option. Requirement numbers are those of the FS (FR-s.n). Detailed requirements added here are numbered DR-s.n by section of this document. Acceptance tests are AT-s.n. Risks are K-n; analyst questions are Q-n. Data structures are given as JSON with comments (//), which JSON itself does not allow; the files themselves carry none. Interfaces are given as JavaScript signatures. Lengths are in millimetres unless said otherwise; canvas coordinates are in pixels, y downward.

1.4 What is settled and what is not

Decisions recorded with the owner are D-1 to D-15 in the FS (section 4.2). Open items are O-1 to O-16 (FS section 12). This document does not settle open items; where a design depends on one, both branches are specified and marked.

2.0 CONTEXT AND CONSTRAINTS

2.1 The owner and the work

The owner is a retired technical writer and an old-time Unix maintenance programmer (Xerox, Sun, Stellar, TotalView, NobleNet). Sketchpad is the first program he has written in twelve years; much of it is relearning. He reads every line he keeps, so the code must be plain and readable rather than clever. He works on Windows in VS Code, reviews from an iPad, and uses AI assistants to write code under his rules. Earlier assistants failed him in two ways the design must guard against: deleting code unrelated to the change in hand, and taking a shortcut to the result instead of using the pattern that already existed.

He makes string art: thread wound between nails driven into a board, the threads' envelope forming curves. The classic construction is the corner stitch: two lines of nails meeting at a corner, nail i of one joined to nail i of the other, which draws a parabola. His aim is original work rather than formulaic craft. Sketchpad has two purposes of equal standing (FS 1.2):

  1. Templates. A printable, true-scale point template for driving the nails.
  2. Sketching. A place to explore designs cheaply by working with how objects are represented and how they relate. Making exploration cheap is a major function (D-8).

StringThing (to late 2025)One 4,900-line HTML file: a single StringThing settings object with about 30 defaulted fields, 42 numbered tests switched on by uncommenting a line, and the numbered Figures of the owner's ideabook.Separate the definition of a drawing from how it is drawn. Declare little, default everything, draw whatever is asked (D-15). A point may be referred to by number (new Point(n)), the seed of the V2 point table.
Manager (2 weeks)A manager of StringThing instances.A dead end: managing more copies of a design that cannot grow does not help.
Sketchpad v.1A UI model from the owner's workflow (Draw, Patterns, Gallery, Utilities), a draw registry, manifests.The tabs have barely changed since.
Sketchpad v.2 ("V1" in these documents)Subsystems, categories, Home; then Figures (layers, discs, welds, transforms), print aids, magic points; then error reporting, regression tests and Ideabook hints (November 2026).The UI held; the drawing side, never rethought, is straining (FS 3.3).

The owner's own numbering calls the rebuild Sketchpad 3 (O-11). These documents keep "V1" and "V2".

2.3 Constraints

DR-2.1Plain JavaScript ES modules. No framework, no build step, no transpiler, no TypeScript (A-2). A dev server (Vite) may serve files; the code must also run from a plain static server for read-only review.
DR-2.2A local Node service (one process, one port) performs every file write. The browser never writes files.
DR-2.3Windows is the primary platform; macOS and Linux shall also work (the owner may work from a borrowed Mac or a Linux USB drive). Paths shall be handled with the platform's path module, never by string joining with "/".
DR-2.4Works offline (FR-6.18.7). No CDN at run time.
DR-2.5Readable code: one file per idea, a header comment saying what it does (read by the Notes popup), names that say what they are, no cleverness for its own sake. A function longer than about 60 lines should be split unless splitting hides the idea.
DR-2.6No implicit globals. Shared state is declared in a state object (FS 6.7).
DR-2.7The iPad is for review only (D-2): reading documents and the running app; no authoring.
DR-2.8Everything is in git; small, described commits; a branch per phase, reviewed by the owner before merge.
